Part 2&3 地点 PLACE

Describe a tall building you like or dislike

描述一座你喜欢或不喜欢的高楼

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a tall building you like or dislike

  • What it is used for (它的用途是什么)
  • Where it is (它在哪里)
  • What it looks like (它看起来什么样)
  • And explain why you like/dislike it (并解释为什么你喜欢/不喜欢它)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a tall building you like or dislike

I'd like to talk about a tall building I really dislike, the Ping An Finance Centre in Shenzhen, which is where I live. To start with, it's in the heart of the Futian business district, so I walk past it quite often on my way to work. It's mainly used as an office tower, full of banks and financial companies. In terms of height, it's one of the tallest buildings in the world, around six hundred metres, with more than a hundred floors. As for what it looks like, it's basically a slim glass tower with a pointed top. The whole surface is covered with glass panels that reflect the sky, so it looks elegant from a distance, and at night it's covered in lights, which is quite striking. I have to admit, it's impressive from across the street. The main reason I dislike it, though, is that I'm afraid of heights, and standing next to a building that tall makes me feel really uneasy. I remember once I went up to the observation deck with friends, and as soon as I looked down from the top, my legs went weak and I had to sit down. Since then, I've avoided going anywhere near the top of a tall building. So all in all, I can appreciate that it's a modern landmark, but I personally can't enjoy it because of my fear of heights. For me, it's beautiful from the ground, and that's where my comfort ends.

深圳平安金融中心（约 600 米、100 多层，福田金融区，办公用途）；玻璃幕墙细长塔楼、顶部尖细、夜晚亮灯。因为怕高而不喜欢：曾在观景台向下看腿软，之后避开高楼顶部；虽承认是城市地标，但从地面欣赏就够了。

Q2Are there many tall buildings in your country?

Yes, there are quite a lot, especially in big cities like Shanghai, Shenzhen and Guangzhou. Over the past twenty years, the number of skyscrapers has grown really quickly, mainly because land is scarce and the population keeps rising. In my city, you can see dozens of towers over two hundred metres tall. That said, in smaller cities and rural areas, most buildings are still fairly low.

大城市（上海、深圳、广州）摩天楼很多；近二十年因土地稀缺、人口增长而快速增多；小城市和农村仍以低层建筑为主。

Q3What are the differences between those tall buildings in your country?

I think the differences mainly come down to function and design. Commercial towers, like the Ping An Finance Centre, are built for offices, so they're tall and slim, packed with glass and steel. Residential buildings, on the other hand, tend to be a bit lower and wider, with balconies and apartment windows. Some older towers have a more traditional look, while newer ones are quite futuristic. So really, the design often reflects what the building is used for.

差异主要在功能与设计：写字楼高而细、玻璃钢幕墙；住宅楼较矮较宽、带阳台；新老塔楼风格不同；设计往往反映用途。

Q4Why are different places laid out and designed differently?

I believe it's mainly down to geography, history and the local economy. In coastal or mountainous areas, the land itself shapes how a city is planned, so buildings have to fit the landscape. Cities with a long history, like Beijing, keep narrow old streets, whereas newer cities are designed around wide roads and modern districts. The economy also plays a role, because richer cities can afford grander and taller buildings. So ultimately, every city reflects its own conditions.

主要取决于地理、历史和经济：沿海或山地地形影响布局，古城保留窄老街巷，新城规划宽阔道路，经济实力决定建筑规模与高度。

Q5Why do some people feel nervous when they visit very tall buildings?

I think it's mostly a psychological reaction rather than a real danger. When people stand at a great height, their brain often warns them that something is unsafe, even though they're perfectly safe behind glass. For some people this fear is mild, while for others it's quite strong and hard to control. Having said that, many people actually enjoy the excitement of high places, so I suppose it really depends on the person.

主要是心理反应：站在高处时大脑发出危险信号，即使实际很安全；恐惧程度因人而异，也有人很享受这种刺激。
